sanskrit: etena tūrṇaṃ pratipādayemāñ; śvetān hayān kāñcanaraśmiyoktrān javena sarveṇa kuru prayatnam; āsādayaitad rathasiṃhavṛndam
english: Lead me quickly by this way to those white horses yoked with golden reins; apply every effort with full speed — bring me close to that pride of chariot-lions.

sanskrit: gajo gajeneva mayā durātmā; yo yoddhum ākāṅkṣati sūtaputraḥ tam eva māṃ prāpaya rājaputra; duryodhanāpāśrayajātadarpam
english: That wicked son of a charioteer who desires to fight me — bring me to him, O prince, as elephant meets elephant; his arrogance born of shelter under Duryodhana shall be met.

sanskrit: sa tair hayair vātajavair bṛhadbhiḥ; putro virāṭasya suvarṇakakṣyaiḥ vidhvaṃsayaṃs tadrathinām anīkaṃ; tato 'vahat pāṇḍavam ājimadhye
english: With those great horses swift as wind, girt with golden girths, the son of Virāṭa, scattering the array of the enemy charioteers, then bore the Pāṇḍava into the midst of battle.

sanskrit: taṃ citraseno viśikhair vipāṭhaiḥ; saṃgrāmajic chatrusaho jayaś ca pratyudyayur bhāratam āpatantaṃ; mahārathāḥ karṇam abhīpsamānāḥ
english: Against him as he charged, Citrasena with barbed shafts, Saṃgrāmajit, Śatrusaha, and Jaya — great chariot-warriors desiring to protect Karṇa — rode out against that descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa teṣāṃ puruṣapravīraḥ; śarāsanārciḥ śaravegatāpaḥ vrātān rathānām adahat sa manyur; vanaṃ yathāgniḥ kurupuṃgavānām
english: Then he, foremost of men, blazing with his bow, scorching with the velocity of his arrows, his wrath burnt up the swarms of Kuru bulls' chariots as fire burns a forest.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu yuddhe tumule pravṛtte; pārthaṃ vikarṇo 'tirathaṃ rathena vipāṭhavarṣeṇa kurupravīro; bhīmena bhīmānujam āsasāda
english: While that tumultuous battle raged, Vikarṇa — a great Kuru hero — in his chariot, pouring a rain of piercing shafts, approached Pārtha, that foremost of chariot-fighters, the younger brother of the mighty Bhīma.

sanskrit: tato vikarṇasya dhanur vikṛṣya; jāmbūnadāgryopacitaṃ dṛḍhajyam apātayad dhvajam asya pramathya; chinnadhvajaḥ so 'py apayāj javena
english: Then Arjuna, seizing Vikarṇa's bow — studded with fine gold and fitted with a firm string — brought it down, and smashed his banner; with his banner cut down, Vikarṇa too fled swiftly.

sanskrit: taṃ śātravāṇāṃ gaṇabādhitāraṃ; karmāṇi kurvāṇam amānuṣāṇi śatruṃtapaḥ kopam amṛṣyamāṇaḥ; samarpayat kūrmanakhena pārtham
english: Him who was afflicting the masses of enemies and performing superhuman feats — Śatruṃtapa, unable to endure his anger, assailed Pārtha with a tortoise-nail arrow.

sanskrit: sa tena rājñātirathena viddho; vigāhamāno dhvajinīṃ kurūṇām śatruṃtapaṃ pañcabhir āśu viddhvā; tato 'sya sūtaṃ daśabhir jaghāna
english: Pierced by that king who was a foremost chariot-fighter, Arjuna, plunging deeper into the Kuru host, quickly struck Śatruṃtapa with five arrows and then killed his charioteer with ten.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa viddho bharatarṣabheṇa; bāṇena gātrāvaraṇātigena gatāsur ājau nipapāta bhūmau; nago nagāgrād iva vātarugṇaḥ
english: Then he, pierced by that bull of the Bharatas with an arrow that penetrated his body-armor, fell lifeless upon the field, like a great elephant toppling from a mountain peak uprooted by the wind.

sanskrit: ratharṣabhās te tu ratharṣabheṇa; vīrā raṇe vīratareṇa bhagnāḥ cakampire vātavaśena kāle; prakampitānīva mahāvanāni
english: Those bulls among chariot-warriors, those heroes, broken in battle by that still greater hero, trembled as great forests shaken by the force of the wind in the season of storms.

sanskrit: hatās tu pārthena narapravīrā; bhūmau yuvānaḥ suṣupuḥ suveṣāḥ vasupradā vāsavatulyavīryāḥ; parājitā vāsavajena saṃkhye suvarṇakārṣṇāyasavarmanaddhā; nāgā yathā haimavatāḥ pravṛddhāḥ
english: Slain by Pārtha, those foremost of men lay sleeping on the earth — young, finely dressed, generous with wealth, equal in valor to Indra, defeated in battle by Indra's son — clad in armor of gold and dark iron, like great elephants of the Himalayan slopes.

sanskrit: tathā sa śatrūn samare vinighnan; gāṇḍīvadhanvā puruṣapravīraḥ cacāra saṃkhye pradiśo diśaś ca; dahann ivāgnir vanam ātapānte
english: Thus slaying enemies in battle, the Gāṇḍīva-bowman, foremost of men, ranged the field in all directions and intermediate quarters, like fire burning a forest at the end of summer.

sanskrit: prakīrṇaparṇāni yathā vasante; viśātayitvātyanilo nudan khe tathā sapatnān vikiran kirīṭī; cacāra saṃkhye 'tiratho rathena
english: As the great gale in spring, driving through the sky, strips trees of their scattered leaves, so the Diademed One, scattering his foes, ranged the battlefield as a supreme chariot-warrior on his car.

sanskrit: śoṇāśvavāhasya hayān nihatya; vaikartanabhrātur adīnasattvaḥ ekena saṃgrāmajitaḥ śareṇa; śiro jahārātha kirīṭamālī
english: Having slain the horses of him who drove red horses, the wearer of the diadem — that undaunted soul — with a single arrow cut off the head of Saṃgrāmajit, the brother of the son of Vikartana.

sanskrit: tasmin hate bhrātari sūtaputro; vaikartano vīryam athādadānaḥ pragṛhya dantāv iva nāgarājo; maharṣabhaṃ vyāghra ivābhyadhāvat
english: When his brother was slain, the son of the charioteer — Vaikartana — gathered his valor; like the lord of elephants lifting his tusks, he charged at that great bull like a tiger.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; vaikartanaḥ śīghram upājaghāna vivyādha gātreṣu hayāṃś ca sarvān; virāṭaputraṃ ca śarair nijaghne
english: Vaikartana swiftly struck the Pāṇḍava with twelve winged shafts, pierced his limbs and all his horses, and struck the son of Virāṭa with arrows.

sanskrit: sa hastinevābhihato gajendraḥ; pragṛhya bhallān niśitān niṣaṅgāt ākarṇapūrṇaṃ ca dhanur vikṛṣya; vivyādha bāṇair atha sūtaputram
english: He, like the lord of elephants struck by another elephant, drew sharp bhalla arrows from his quiver, drew his bow to the full extent of his ear, and pierced the son of the charioteer with arrows.

sanskrit: athāsya bāhūruśirolalāṭaṃ; grīvāṃ rathāṅgāni parāvamardī sthitasya bāṇair yudhi nirbibheda; gāṇḍīvamuktair aśaniprakāśaiḥ
english: Then, with arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, bright as thunderbolts, that crusher of foes pierced his arms, thighs, head, forehead, throat, and all the parts of his chariot as he stood in battle.

sanskrit: sa pārthamuktair viśikhaiḥ praṇunno; gajo gajeneva jitas tarasvī vihāya saṃgrāmaśiraḥ prayāto; vaikartanaḥ pāṇḍavabāṇataptaḥ
english: Driven back by the shafts loosed by Pārtha, like a swift elephant vanquished by another elephant, scorched by the arrows of the Pāṇḍava, Vaikartana abandoned the foremost of the battle and departed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca apayāte tu rādheye duryodhanapurogamāḥ anīkena yathāsvena śarair ārcchanta pāṇḍavam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the son of Rādhā had retreated, the warriors led by Duryodhana attacked the Pāṇḍava with their respective divisions with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: bahudhā tasya sainyasya vyūḍhasyāpatataḥ śaraiḥ abhiyānīyam ājñāya vairāṭir idam abravīt
english: Recognizing which of those many divisions of his army advancing in array with arrows was to be confronted, the son of Virāṭa spoke these words.

sanskrit: āsthāya ruciraṃ jiṣṇo rathaṃ sārathinā mayā katamad yāsyase 'nīkam ukto yāsyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: "I, as charioteer, have mounted this splendid chariot, O Jiṣṇu — tell me, which division will you go to? I shall go wherever you direct me."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca lohitākṣam ariṣṭaṃ yaṃ vaiyāghram anupaśyasi nīlāṃ patākām āśritya rathe tiṣṭhantam uttara
english: Arjuna said: "Do you see that one, O Uttara, with red eyes, auspicious, wearing a tiger skin, standing in his chariot under a dark blue banner — bring me to him."

sanskrit: kṛpasyaitad rathānīkaṃ prāpayasvaitad eva mām etasya darśayiṣyāmi śīghrāstraṃ dṛḍhadhanvinaḥ
english: "That is the chariot-force of Kṛpa — bring me to that very one. I shall demonstrate to this firm-bowed man my swift mastery of weapons."

sanskrit: kamaṇḍalur dhvaje yasya śātakumbhamayaḥ śubhaḥ ācārya eṣa vai droṇaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: "He on whose banner a beautiful water-pot of gold is displayed — that teacher is Droṇa himself, best among all who bear arms."

sanskrit: suprasannamanā vīra kuruṣvainaṃ pradakṣiṇam atraiva cāvirodhena eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: "With a glad mind, O hero, circumambulate him to the right — here and without obstruction; this is the eternal rule of righteousness."

sanskrit: yadi me prathamaṃ droṇaḥ śarīre prahariṣyati tato 'sya prahariṣyāmi nāsya kopo bhaviṣyati
english: "If Droṇa strikes my body first, then I will strike him in return — and he will not be angry at that."

sanskrit: asyāvidūre tu dhanur dhvajāgre yasya dṛśyate ācāryasyaiṣa putro vai aśvatthāmā mahārathaḥ
english: "Not far from him, the one whose bow is visible at the top of his banner — that is the teacher's son, Aśvatthāmā, a great chariot-warrior."

sanskrit: sadā mamaiṣa mānyaś ca sarvaśastrabhṛtām api etasya tvaṃ rathaṃ prāpya nivartethāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "He is always to be honored by me, and by all who bear arms. Having reached his chariot, you must turn back again and again without engaging him."

sanskrit: ya eṣa tu rathānīke suvarṇakavacāvṛtaḥ senāgryeṇa tṛtīyena vyavahāryeṇa tiṣṭhati
english: "He who stands there in the chariot array, clad in golden armor, at the head of the third division of the army, in the battle formation —"

sanskrit: yasya nāgo dhvajāgre vai hemaketanasaṃśritaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajaḥ śrīmān eṣa rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: "He on whose banner-top an elephant is displayed, set upon a golden standard — that resplendent son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is King Suyodhana."

sanskrit: etasyābhimukhaṃ vīra rathaṃ pararathārujaḥ prāpayasvaiṣa tejobhipramāthī yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: "Turn the chariot to face him, O hero who shatters enemy chariots — bring me to him; this one destroys brilliance and is maddened in battle."

sanskrit: eṣa droṇasya śiṣyāṇāṃ śīghrāstraḥ prathamo mataḥ etasya darśayiṣyāmi śīghrāstraṃ vipulaṃ śaraiḥ
english: "He is considered the foremost in swift archery among Droṇa's disciples. I shall demonstrate to him my vast swiftness with arrows."

sanskrit: nāgakakṣyā tu rucirā dhvajāgre yasya tiṣṭhati eṣa vaikartanaḥ karṇo viditaḥ pūrvam eva te
english: "He whose beautiful serpent-girth stands atop his banner — that is Vaikartana Karṇa, known to you already."

sanskrit: etasya ratham āsthāya rādheyasya durātmanaḥ yatto bhavethāḥ saṃgrāme spardhaty eṣa mayā sadā
english: "Approaching the chariot of this wicked son of Rādhā, you must be vigilant in battle — he always contends with me as a rival."

sanskrit: yas tu nīlānusāreṇa pañcatāreṇa ketunā hastāvāpī bṛhaddhanvā rathe tiṣṭhati vīryavān
english: "He who stands in his chariot, mighty, bearing arm-guards, with a great bow, under a banner that is blue adorned with five stars —"

sanskrit: yasya tārārkacitro 'sau rathe dhvajavaraḥ sthitaḥ yasyaitat pāṇḍuraṃ chatraṃ vimalaṃ mūrdhni tiṣṭhati
english: "He whose finest banner on his chariot is adorned with stars and the sun, and above whose head stands that white, spotless parasol —"

sanskrit: mahato rathavaṃśasya nānādhvajapatākinaḥ balāhakāgre sūryo vā ya eṣa pramukhe sthitaḥ
english: "He who stands at the forefront of that great chariot lineage with its many banners and pennants, like the sun at the head of the Balāhaka clouds —"

sanskrit: haimaṃ candrārkasaṃkāśaṃ kavacaṃ yasya dṛśyate jātarūpaśirastrāṇas trāsayann iva me manaḥ
english: "He whose golden armor shines like the moon and sun, whose helmet is of pure gold — he fills my heart with something like awe."

sanskrit: eṣa śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ sarveṣāṃ naḥ pitāmahaḥ rājaśriyāvabaddhas tu duryodhanavaśānugaḥ
english: "This is Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, grandsire of us all — though bound by the royal fortune and following in obedience to Duryodhana."

sanskrit: paścād eṣa prayātavyo na me vighnakaro bhavet etena yudhyamānasya yattaḥ saṃyaccha me hayān
english: "He is to be approached last, lest he become an obstacle to me. While I fight with these others, hold my horses steady and attentive."

sanskrit: tato 'bhyavahad avyagro vairāṭiḥ savyasācinam yatrātiṣṭhat kṛpo rājan yotsyamāno dhanaṃjayam
english: Then the son of Virāṭa, unperturbed, drove the Left-handed Archer to where Kṛpa stood, O King, ready to do battle with Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tāny anīkāny adṛśyanta kurūṇām ugradhanvinām saṃsarpanto yathā meghā gharmānte mandamārutāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The armies of the Kurus, terrible with their bows, could be seen creeping forward like clouds driven by gentle winds at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: abhyāśe vājinas tasthuḥ samārūḍhāḥ prahāribhiḥ bhīmarūpāś ca mātaṅgās tomarāṅkuśacoditāḥ
english: Nearby, horses stood mounted by fighters, and terrible-looking elephants were urged on with lances and goads.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraḥ suragaṇaiḥ samāruhya sudarśanam sahopāyāt tadā rājan viśvāśvimarutāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: Then Śakra, mounting Sudarśana together with hosts of gods, arrived there, O King, with the Viśvas, the Aśvins, and the troops of Maruts.

sanskrit: tad devayakṣagandharvamahoragasamākulam śuśubhe 'bhravinirmuktaṃ grahair iva nabhastalam
english: That sky, thronged with gods, yakṣas, gandharvas, and great serpents, and freed from clouds, shone like the heavens adorned with planets.

sanskrit: astrāṇāṃ ca balaṃ teṣāṃ mānuṣeṣu prayujyatām tac ca ghoraṃ mahad yuddhaṃ bhīṣmārjunasamāgame
english: And the power of those divine weapons as they were employed against humans, and that terrible great battle at the encounter between Bhīṣma and Arjuna —

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ yatra sthūṇā hiraṇmayāḥ maṇiratnamayāś cānyāḥ prāsādam upadhārayan
english: — where a hundred times a hundred thousand golden pillars, and others made of jewels and precious stones, supported a palace —

sanskrit: tatra kāmagamaṃ divyaṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitam vimānaṃ devarājasya śuśubhe khecaraṃ tadā
english: — there the celestial sky-going palace of the king of gods, adorned with all manner of gems, going wherever its master willed, shone beautifully in the air.

sanskrit: tatra devās trayastriṃśat tiṣṭhanti sahavāsavāḥ gandharvā rākṣasāḥ sarpāḥ pitaraś ca maharṣibhiḥ
english: There stood the thirty-three gods together with Vāsava, gandharvas, rākṣasas, serpents, and the ancestors along with great sages.

sanskrit: tathā rājā vasumanā balākṣaḥ supratardanaḥ aṣṭakaś ca śibiś caiva yayātir nahuṣo gayaḥ
english: And likewise King Vasumanas, Balākṣa, Supratardana, Aṣṭaka, Śibi, Yayāti, Nahuṣa, and Gaya —

sanskrit: manuḥ kṣupo raghur bhānuḥ kṛśāśvaḥ sagaraḥ śalaḥ vimāne devarājasya samadṛśyanta suprabhāḥ
english: — Manu, Kṣupa, Raghu, Bhānu, Kṛśāśva, Sagara, and Śala — all were to be seen, radiant, in the palace of the king of gods.

sanskrit: agner īśasya somasya varuṇasya prajāpateḥ tathā dhātur vidhātuś ca kuberasya yamasya ca
english: The celestial vehicles of Agni, Īśa, Soma, Varuṇa, Prajāpati, of Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, of Kubera, and of Yama —

sanskrit: alambusograsenasya gandharvasya ca tumburoḥ yathābhāgaṃ yathoddeśaṃ vimānāni cakāśire
english: — and of Alambusa, Ugrasena, and the gandharva Tumburu — each in its proper place and according to its allotted station, the celestial cars shone resplendent.

sanskrit: sarvadevanikāyāś ca siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ arjunasya kurūṇāṃ ca draṣṭuṃ yuddham upāgatāḥ
english: All the hosts of gods, the siddhas, and the greatest sages had come to witness the battle between Arjuna and the Kurus.

sanskrit: divyānāṃ tatra mālyānāṃ gandhaḥ puṇyo 'tha sarvaśaḥ prasasāra vasantāgre vanānām iva puṣpitām
english: There the pure fragrance of divine garlands spread in all directions, as the scent of blooming forests spreads at the onset of spring.

sanskrit: raktāraktāni devānāṃ samadṛśyanta tiṣṭhatām ātapatrāṇi vāsāṃsi srajaś ca vyajanāni ca
english: Of the gods as they stood there, their red and non-red parasols, garments, garlands, and fans were all to be seen.

sanskrit: upaśāmyad rajo bhaumaṃ sarvaṃ vyāptaṃ marīcibhiḥ divyān gandhān upādāya vāyur yodhān asevata
english: The earthly dust subsided, all was pervaded by rays of light, and the wind, carrying divine fragrances, attended upon the warriors.

sanskrit: prabhāsitam ivākāśaṃ citrarūpam alaṃkṛtam saṃpatadbhiḥ sthitaiś caiva nānāratnāvabhāsitaiḥ vimānair vividhaiś citrair upānītaiḥ surottamaiḥ
english: The sky shone brilliantly, adorned with wonderful forms — illuminated by the many jewels of the various brilliant celestial cars, of every kind and pattern, brought there by the greatest of the gods, some flying, others stationed still.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etasminn antare tatra mahāvīryaparākramaḥ ājagāma mahāsattvaḥ kṛpaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ arjunaṃ prati saṃyoddhuṃ yuddhārthī sa mahārathaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At that juncture, the great-souled Kṛpa — of great might and valor, best of those who bear arms — arrived, that great chariot-warrior, desirous of battle, to fight against Arjuna.

sanskrit: tau rathau sūryasaṃkāśau yotsyamānau mahābalau śāradāv iva jīmūtau vyarocetāṃ vyavasthitau
english: Those two chariots, bright as the sun, of those two mighty warriors poised to fight, shone brilliantly where they stood like two autumn clouds.

sanskrit: pārtho 'pi viśrutaṃ loke gāṇḍīvaṃ paramāyudham vikṛṣya cikṣepa bahūn nārācān marmabhedinaḥ
english: Pārtha too, drawing the Gāṇḍīva — that supreme weapon renowned throughout the world — loosed many iron shafts that pierced to the vital points.

sanskrit: tān aprāptāñ śitair bāṇair nārācān raktabhojanān kṛpaś ciccheda pārthasya śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Those iron arrows, feeders on blood, before they even arrived — Kṛpa cut them with his sharp shafts, by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthaś ca saṃkruddhaś citrān mārgān pradarśayan diśaḥ saṃchādayan bāṇaiḥ pradiśaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, enraged, displaying varied trajectories and covering all directions and intermediate quarters with arrows, that great chariot-warrior —

sanskrit: ekacchāyam ivākāśaṃ prakurvan sarvataḥ prabhuḥ pracchādayad ameyātmā pārthaḥ śaraśataiḥ kṛpam
english: — making the sky as if of one uniform shade on all sides, that measureless-souled lord Pārtha covered Kṛpa with hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: sa śarair arpitaḥ kruddhaḥ śitair agniśikhopamaiḥ tūrṇaṃ śarasahasreṇa pārtham apratimaujasam arpayitvā mahātmānaṃ nanāda samare kṛpaḥ
english: Struck with those sharp arrows like flames of fire and angered, Kṛpa swiftly struck that great-souled Pārtha — of matchless energy — with a thousand arrows in return, and then roared in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhāgrair vīraḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ tvaran gāṇḍīvanirmuktair arjunas tasya vājinaḥ caturbhiś caturas tīkṣṇair avidhyat parameṣubhiḥ
english: Then the hero Arjuna, with haste, shot from the Gāṇḍīva arrows tipped with gold, with smooth joints, four supreme shafts — piercing each of his four horses with one each.

sanskrit: te hayā niśitair viddhā jvaladbhir iva pannagaiḥ utpetuḥ sahasā sarve kṛpaḥ sthānād athācyavat
english: Those horses, pierced by sharp arrows like blazing serpents, all leaped up at once, and Kṛpa was dislodged from his position.

sanskrit: cyutaṃ tu gautamaṃ sthānāt samīkṣya kurunandanaḥ nāvidhyat paravīraghno rakṣamāṇo 'sya gauravam
english: But seeing Gautama Kṛpa dislodged from his position, the joy of the Kurus — that slayer of enemy heroes — did not strike him, respecting his dignity.

sanskrit: sa tu labdhvā punaḥ sthānaṃ gautamaḥ savyasācinam vivyādha daśabhir bāṇais tvaritaḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: But Gautama Kṛpa, having regained his footing, swiftly pierced the Left-handed Archer with ten arrows feathered with heron-plumes.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho dhanus tasya bhallena niśitena ca cicchedaikena bhūyaś ca hastāc cāpam athāharat
english: Then Pārtha cut his bow with a single sharp bhalla arrow, and then again wrested the bow from his hand.

sanskrit: athāsya kavacaṃ bāṇair niśitair marmabhedibhiḥ vyadhaman na ca pārtho 'sya śarīram avapīḍayat
english: Then with sharp arrows that pierced to the vital spots, Pārtha struck his armor — yet Pārtha did not wound his body itself.

sanskrit: tasya nirmucyamānasya kavacāt kāya ābabhau samaye mucyamānasya sarpasyeva tanur yathā
english: As his armor fell away from him, his body shone forth, like the body of a serpent at the fitting moment as it sloughs its skin.

sanskrit: chinne dhanuṣi pārthena so 'nyad ādāya kārmukam cakāra gautamaḥ sajyaṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: When his bow was cut by Pārtha, Gautama Kṛpa took up another and strung it — and that seemed wondrous indeed.

sanskrit: sa tad apy asya kaunteyaś ciccheda nataparvaṇā evam anyāni cāpāni bahūni kṛtahastavat śāradvatasya ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ paravīrahā
english: The son of Kuntī cut that one too with a smooth-jointed shaft; and thus many other bows as well the Pāṇḍava, slayer of enemy heroes, cut with skilled hands — those of Śaradvatī's son one after another.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanur ādāya atha śaktiṃ pratāpavān prāhiṇot pāṇḍuputrāya pradīptām aśanīm iva
english: Then, his bow cut away, the valiant one took up a lance and hurled it at the son of Pāṇḍu, blazing like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tām arjunas tadāyāntīṃ śaktiṃ hemavibhūṣitām viyadgatāṃ maholkābhāṃ ciccheda daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ sāpatad daśadhā chinnā bhūmau pārthena dhīmatā
english: That lance as it came — adorned with gold, soaring through the sky, bright as a great meteor — Arjuna cut with ten arrows; falling in ten pieces, it was cut to the ground by the wise Pārtha.

sanskrit: yugamadhye tu bhallais tu tataḥ sa sadhanuḥ kṛpaḥ tam āśu niśitaiḥ pārthaṃ bibheda daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, in the middle of the yoke, with bhalla arrows, Kṛpa — his bow now restored — swiftly pierced Pārtha with ten sharp shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahātejā viśikhān agnitejasaḥ cikṣepa samare kruddhas trayodaśa śilāśitān
english: Then Pārtha, of great splendor, enraged in battle, released thirteen arrows sharpened on stone, blazing with the fire of their energy.
